rationale: The fixed experiment 8086d0fc533a4eabb061df6601d55b5b-experiment executed (receipt 97ac203cae5841dfbe14ff058bd7fe95, completed, exit 0) and I read its receipt before writing anything. The raw parsed events show exactly the two behaviors the source account predicted, but the comparison machinery returned unknown for both comparisons because I gave the two probe events the same name (read_ack_probe) and the two setups the same name (read_ack_setup); the controller then cross-correlated them, reporting for comparison 0 that event 3 lacked a matching prerequisite (setup_oversized) while comparison 0 had only event 1. So this turn (a) records an honest interpretation of the existing receipt: observed output consistent with the source account, but no completed comparison, because the harness identity construction - not the target - caused the unknown outcome; and (b) submits a revised experiment with per-case event names so each comparison has an unambiguous admission. The revision needs fresh execution, as required when the harness basis changes.

scope.description: Exercise the unexported readOnly confirmation path of package raft with ack values the live instance's heartbeatCtx never emitted, and record the two candidate consequences: an out-of-range slice in maybeAdvance, and confirmation of reads that the acking voter never observed.
assumptions: ack positions are supplied directly to readOnly.recvAck, standing in for MsgHeartbeatResp.Context values; this is an out-of-contract input, since the library's own follower path echoes the leader's context (see a167f4c33dc94f34b03ea29dbe7ec15a-knowledge-0).
ReadOnlySafe option; three voters (1,2,3) so the quorum position is the median of the stored acks.
The self-ack of the leader (id 1) is produced by heartbeatCtx() exactly as sendMsgReadIndexResponse does it.
excluded: Any claim that a legal cluster produces these inputs; the experiment characterises the code, not reachability.
Lease-based reads, which do not use the ack map.

experiment.prefix: Each test builds a fresh readOnly via newReadOnly(ReadOnlySafe), admits one or two MsgReadIndex stand-ins through readOnly.addRequest(committedIndex, msg), self-acks with readOnly.recvAck(leaderID, readOnly.heartbeatCtx()), then injects peer acks with readOnly.recvAck(peerID, littleEndianUint64(position)) using values the leader never emitted, and finally calls readOnly.maybeAdvance(quorum.JointConfig with Voters[0]={1,2,3}). No raft instance, network or storage is involved; the ack map, unconfirmedReads and confirmedReads are read directly, and the maybeAdvance call in the oversized case is wrapped in a recover so the panic is recorded as data instead of failing the test.

comparisons.description: When the quorum ack position exceeds the number of outstanding read requests, maybeAdvance slices unconfirmedReads out of range and panics.
One forged ack value combined with the leader's self-ack reaches a 2-of-3 quorum position, so both admitted reads are confirmed although voter 3 never received a heartbeat carrying position 2.

knowledge.assertion: no in-model producer supplies a Context the live leader never emitted, which is why this experiment uses an out-of-contract input
recvAck stores the peer Context as a raw read position and maybeAdvance slices unconfirmedReads by the quorum position without validating the value
every legal Context producer echoes the live leader's emitted value, so the out-of-range precondition has no in-model trigger

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 97ac203cae5841dfbe14ff058bd7fe95 (experiment 8086d0fc533a4eabb061df6601d55b5b-experiment, status completed, exit 0, stderr empty, no changed target files) ran the harness in the isolated workspace with -run ^TestAssurance. Decisive parsed indices: index 1 is the oversized-case probe event with panicked=true and the recorded panic text 'runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:1099511627776] with capacity 1'; index 3 is the forged-case probe event with advanced=2 and confirmed_reads=2, whose admission is index 2 (read_requests=2, leader_ack_position=2, honest_ack_position=1, forged_ack_position=2). Admission events are indices 0 and 2. Those raw values match the source prediction exactly: with a quorum of ack positions larger than the outstanding read count, maybeAdvance slices unconfirmedReads out of range, and with one ack at position 2 that the voter never received, the leader's self-ack plus that value is already a 2-of-3 quorum position, so both admitted reads are confirmed. What I must not claim: the receipt's comparisons did not complete. observations.json reports outcome unknown for comparison 0 (evaluated index 1, missing index 3, reason 'No corresponding prerequisite events reached: setup_oversized/read_ack_setup') and unknown for comparison 1 (evaluated index 3, missing index 1). The cause is my harness, not the target: I gave both probe events the same name and both setups the same name, so the controller cross-correlated the cases and each comparison saw a probe event whose prerequisite was the other case's. I therefore record observed output consistent with the account but no completed comparison, and the successor experiment submitted alongside this record gives each case distinct event names so the identities are unambiguous. The source understanding is unchanged and the defect claim stays refuted: the precondition is still a Context the live instance never emitted, which a167f4c33dc94f34b03ea29dbe7ec15a-knowledge-0 shows has no in-model producer, so this receipt demonstrates code behavior under an out-of-contract input rather than a reachable consensus defect. Unchanged uncertainty, still unclaimed: addRequest does not deduplicate by request context, so documented ReadIndex retries with an identical context accumulate one unconfirmed entry and one heartbeat broadcast each while the leader cannot reach a quorum ack.
limitations: The comparisons for this receipt are unknown because of harness identity construction (duplicate event names), so this revision cites raw parsed indices as observed output and does not claim a satisfied comparison.
The experiment injects ack values directly into the unexported readOnly, so it characterises the code path under an out-of-contract input and establishes no network reachability.
The refutation of the in-model premise remains a source argument (readOnly lifetime and Context producer enumeration); no execution in this run tests it.
